extracted.subtask_description: TMLR's guidelines for action editors (AEs) describe each step of the AE workflow: accepting assignments within quota, desk-rejecting inappropriate submissions, assigning and managing reviewers, running the post-review discussion, and producing a decision recommendation aligned with the TMLR acceptance criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: AE annual quota and rolling assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: AE assignments are given on a rolling basis, as submissions are received. The default quota is 12 papers per year, but it is possible to change it through the openreview console, as well as to mark yourself temporarily unavailable for periods such as illness, vacation or work leave.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Quota defaults to 12 papers/year; AEs may adjust it or mark themselves unavailable when needed, but assignments are otherwise distributed on a rolling basis.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default expectation to accept in-expertise assignments
rubrics_metrics.description: On the other hand, you are generally expected to accept all AE requests of submissions that fall within your expertise and quota. Acceptable exceptions are if you have a conflict of interest with one of the authors.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Within their quota and expertise, AEs are expected to accept assignments; declining is only acceptable in the case of a conflict of interest with an author.

rubrics_metrics.name: Desk-rejection decision within one week
rubrics_metrics.description: The first step following an AE assignment is to determine (within 1 week) whether or not the submitted preprint is appropriate for TMLR and respects our submission guidelines.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs must make an initial appropriateness / desk-rejection determination within one week of assignment.

rubrics_metrics.name: Clear desk-rejection cases (anonymization, stylefile, overlap)
rubrics_metrics.description: Clear cases of desk rejection include submissions that are not anonymized, submissions that do not use the unmodified TMLR stylefile and submissions that clearly overlap with work already published in proceedings (or currently under review for publication).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Three explicit desk-reject triggers: (1) missing anonymization, (2) modified or wrong stylefile (for standard PDF submissions only), (3) clear overlap with work already published or under review elsewhere.

rubrics_metrics.name: Stylefile requirement applies only to standard PDF submissions
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that this stylefile requirement only applies to standard PDF submissions, *not* Beyond PDF submissions. Please check carefully the *submission type* on OpenReview, under the abstract. Standard submissions can have types "long" or "regular." Beyond PDF submission have a separate submission type, "Beyond PDF submission (pageless, webpage-style content)," that should not be confused with standard PDF submissions.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs must check the submission type on OpenReview before applying the stylefile rule; Beyond PDF (pageless, webpage-style) submissions are exempt.

rubrics_metrics.name: Other valid desk-rejection grounds
rubrics_metrics.description: There are other reasons a submission may be desk rejected, including (but not limited to) lack of fit with the scope of TMLR, lack of expertise in the TMLR reviewer pool to evaluate the submission, low likelihood that the submission will meet the acceptance criteria of TMLR (e.g., due to lack of technical depth).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Beyond the clear cases, AEs may desk-reject for scope mismatch, lack of expert reviewers in the pool, or apparent inability to meet acceptance criteria due to insufficient technical depth.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consult Editors-in-Chief when unsure about desk-rejection
rubrics_metrics.description: If you are suspect but are unsure whether a submission may need to be desk rejected for any reason, simply reach out to the Editors in Chief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Borderline desk-rejection calls should be escalated to the Editors-in-Chief rather than decided unilaterally.

rubrics_metrics.name: AE identity disclosed to authors at desk-rejection stage
rubrics_metrics.description: Note that your identity as the AE responsible for the submission is known to the authors at that stage. Once you've confirmed that a submission is appropriate for TMLR, the submission becomes public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs should be aware that their identity is visible to authors during the desk-rejection stage and that submissions only become public after the AE confirms appropriateness.

rubrics_metrics.name: Assign three reviewers within one week
rubrics_metrics.description: Once confirmed that a submission is appropriate for TMLR, you should assign it for review to 3 reviewers. You must make the initial assignment within a week of accepting a paper's assignment.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Initial assignment is fixed at three reviewers, and the assignment must be made within one week of the AE accepting the paper.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid over-quota or backlogged reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: However make sure to avoid reviewers who 1) have already filled their annual quota or 2) have an unsubmitted review, unless you've received confirmation from the reviewer that they are willing to take on this additional review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two filters on reviewer choice: skip those at quota and those with outstanding reviews, unless they explicitly confirm willingness to take on more.

rubrics_metrics.name: Default two-week review window; extend for long papers
rubrics_metrics.description: By default, reviewers are asked to submit their review within 2 weeks of their assignment. However, if the submission is longer than 12 pages (excluding any appendix), we ask you to permit a longer reviewing time frame.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Two-week default review window; AEs should grant extensions when the main text exceeds 12 pages (excluding appendix).

rubrics_metrics.name: Vetting volunteer reviewers
rubrics_metrics.description: Some reviewers may proactively reach out to you through OpenReview and volunteer to review the work, and it is up to you to determine whether their review would be valuable for coming to a good decision for the submission. Though OpenReview will provide some basic mechanism to disallow undesirable conflicts of interests, it is your responsibility to ensure that the volunteer reviewer isn't indeed in conflict with the authors of the submission and that they have the appropriate expertise to provide a valuable judgement on the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs bear personal responsibility for screening volunteer reviewers for both conflicts of interest and topical expertise, beyond what OpenReview automatically catches.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject volunteer reviewers with weak OpenReview profiles
rubrics_metrics.description: For instance, do not accept a volunteer reviewer with a profile that is incomplete, out of date or solely based on an unrecognizable personal email (as opposed to an institutional email).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Concrete vetting rule: reject volunteers whose OpenReview profiles are incomplete, out of date, or backed only by an unrecognizable personal email.

rubrics_metrics.name: Track reviewer acknowledgement of assignment
rubrics_metrics.description: Once assigned, reviewers will be asked to acknowledge on OpenReview their responsibility to review this submission. This acknowledgement will be made visible to you on the OpenReview page of the submission. If the reviewer has not acknowledged their responsibility a couple of days after their assignment, consider reaching out to them directly to confirm.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs should monitor reviewer acknowledgements on OpenReview and reach out directly if a reviewer has not acknowledged within a couple of days.

rubrics_metrics.name: Drive active discussion in post-review phase
rubrics_metrics.description: Once the third review has been submitted, the authors are given a chance to take into account the reviewers' feedback, answer any questions they may have asked and update their manuscript accordingly. You are responsible for making sure the reviewers engage actively in this discussion.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: After the third review comes in, the AE is responsible for ensuring reviewers participate actively in the author-reviewer discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: AE may participate in discussion to reach consensus
rubrics_metrics.description: You may also participate in the discussion yourself, by asking questions directly to the authors or starting a private conversation via OpenReview involving only the reviewers to try to reach a consensus, if possible.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs are allowed to intervene directly with authors or hold private reviewer-only conversations to drive consensus.

rubrics_metrics.name: Incorporate relevant non-reviewer signed comments
rubrics_metrics.description: Since papers on OpenReview are visible to all, there might even be signed comments from non-reviewers that you think are relevant and would like to ask authors to react to. Overall, any intervention that will help you come to a decision recommendation for the submission is encouraged (as long as it maintains the anonymity of the authors and reviewers).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs may surface relevant signed public comments from non-reviewers and ask authors to respond, as long as anonymity of authors and reviewers is preserved.

rubrics_metrics.name: Handle ethics concerns via Broader Impact and EiC escalation
rubrics_metrics.description: Our Ethics Guidelines describe TMLR's ethical principles and establish common ground for editors, reviewers, and authors to evaluate the potential for harm of a proposed work. If you or any of the reviewers have concerns around the ethical implications of the submission, check whether the authors address the concerns in the (otherwise optional) Broader Impact Statement section of their preprint. In a situation where you would like an additional reviewer with ethics expertise, or if you suspect that no statement would make the work ethically acceptable, reach out to the Editors-in-Chief.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Process for ethics concerns: first check the Broader Impact Statement; escalate to EiC to obtain an ethics-expert reviewer or to consider rejection on ethical grounds.

rubrics_metrics.name: Discussion window: 2-4 weeks after third review
rubrics_metrics.description: Based on their discussion with the authors, reviewers will submit their own recommendation to you on a decision for a submission no sooner than 2 weeks and no later than 4 weeks after the submission of the third review.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewer decision recommendations are bounded between 2 and 4 weeks after the third review is submitted.

rubrics_metrics.name: AE decision proposal within one week of recommendations
rubrics_metrics.description: Once all 3 reviewer decision recommendations have been submitted, you should aim to submit your decision proposal within 1 week. Your decision proposal should therefore be submitted within 5 weeks of the beginning of the discussion between authors and reviewers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Hard target: AE decision within one week of receiving all three reviewer recommendations (i.e., within five weeks of the start of the author-reviewer discussion).

rubrics_metrics.name: Extension allowed only if discussion ongoing
rubrics_metrics.description: If, and only if, authors and reviewers are still discussing the submission, you may decide to take more time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The only acceptable reason to exceed the AE decision window is an active, ongoing author-reviewer discussion.

rubrics_metrics.name: Three possible decision outcomes
rubrics_metrics.description: There are 3 possible outcomes: Accept, Accept with minor revision and Reject (see Editorial Policies).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AE decision must be one of: Accept, Accept with minor revision, or Reject; defined in the TMLR Editorial Policies.

rubrics_metrics.name: Decisions grounded in the two TMLR acceptance criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: As described in the Acceptance criteria page, acceptance decisions should be made based on two criteria: (1) Are the claims made in the submission supported by accurate, convincing and clear evidence? (2) Would at least some individuals in TMLR's audience be interested in the findings of this paper?
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AE decisions must be tied back to the two TMLR acceptance criteria (evidence-supported claims and at least some audience interest).

rubrics_metrics.name: Optional certification recommendation for accepted papers
rubrics_metrics.description: In addition to a decision, for accepted papers, you may also recommend a certification if you think the paper deserves to stand out with one such additional recognition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: AEs may, but are not required to, recommend certifications (e.g., Featured, Outstanding) for accepted papers that they think merit additional recognition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Verify camera-ready compliance
rubrics_metrics.description: As your final task for an accepted paper, you are asked to quickly verify that the camera ready manuscript complies with TMLR stylefile, with all author information inserted in the manuscript as well as the link to the OpenReview page for the submission.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Camera-ready check covers three items: correct TMLR stylefile, included author information, and a link to the OpenReview page.
